summary: To address the NASA Space Apps "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge, we developed Cosmic Crisp, a 3-dimensional, holistic decision-support platform that translates NASA Earth observations—including Landsat, SMAP, GRACE-FO, and NASA POWER—into practical, farm-level guidance for crop rotation, irrigation contingencies, and pest and disease control. Today, farmers face a critical Crop Rotation Information Gap, making high-stakes planting decisions based on delayed historical intuition that no longer fits shifting temperatures, unpredictable rainfall, and declining soil health. Cosmic Crisp bridges this gap by harmonizing satellite telemetry on groundwater loss, soil moisture anomalies, and heat stress with local field conditions to recommend diversified, climate-resilient rotations that interrupt pest cycles, manage drought or drainage stress, and respect farmer priorities rather than flooding growers with raw weather alerts. By letting farmers compare adaptive scenarios against monocultures without replacing local judgment, Cosmic Crisp delivers transformative impact: boosting yields and revenue by ~20%, cutting nitrogen use by 43–57%, slashing herbicide runoff by 81–96%, and reducing nitrous oxide emissions by up to 49%. Ultimately, turning space-based climate intelligence into clear pre-planting decisions protects generational livelihoods against severe weather losses while advancing UN Sustainable Development Goals 2, 6, 13, and 15.
details: Cosmic Crisp is an offline-first, Space-to-Soil decision-support platform designed for the NASA Space Apps "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge to help farmers adapt to shifting climates and water scarcity. Rather than forcing growers to rely on static farming almanacs or raw weather portals that fail when rural cell signals drop, the application links three critical operational pillars on a single farm profile: Crop Rotation & Economics, Water-Scarcity Irrigation, and Climate-Pathology Pest Strategy.Under the hood, Cosmic Crisp functions as a Progressive Web App (PWA) built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and an Express/Node.js backend (alongside @google/genai and vite-plugin-pwa), ingesting live orbital and environmental telemetry from NASA POWER (5-year climate normals), NASA SMAP L4 (root-zone soil moisture), GPM (rainfall), NASADEM (terrain slope), ISRIC SoilGrids (soil chemistry and texture), FAO EcoCrop (88 crop species), USDA CropScape, NOAA CPC's Oceanic Niño Index (ONI), and 51-member 6-month seasonal ensemble forecasts. By running this multi-mission data through a hydro-pathology engine—and caching satellite bundles and checklists locally using Workbox Service Workers and an IndexedDB sync queue—the platform translates planetary anomalies into local, offline-ready parcel decisions in seconds.Across water, agronomic, economic, and rural-resilience dimensions, Cosmic Crisp delivers clear, measurable benefits:Water Conservation: Balances 6-month evapotranspiration (ETc) against rainfall under ENSO anomalies to shift scarce parcels from 54%-efficient flood furrows to 82%-efficient Rain Pipes or 92%-efficient Drip/SDI, cutting evaporation waste while accounting for extreme storm bursts.Targeted Pest & Crop Economics: Ranks next-cycle rotation crops by soil nitrogen, climate stability, and net margin ROI, while replacing reactive calendar fungicide sprays with pre-season Integrated Pest Management (IPM) triggers (such as staging blue sticky traps and Beauveria bassiana or Neem bio-controls when dry El Niño skies suppress Downy Mildew but drive thrips and mites).Last-Mile Accessibility: Supports 5 languages (EN, ES, HI, FR, PT), both Imperial and Metric units, and 100% offline synchronization so edits persist in zero-signal fields.Ultimately, we hope to bridge the last-mile gap between orbital Earth science and everyday harvest security, empowering farmers worldwide (across regions like the US Corn Belt, Pacific Northwest, California Central Valley, and South Asian monsoon belts) to anticipate climate shocks before losses hit their canopies, protect family livelihoods, and advance sustainable global agriculture.
